source_snapshot.criteria: Readable/correct response without error; SUT should be `ForceRestart`.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; posts to the ComputerSystem member instead of the Reset action, uses `-k`, CLI secrets, fixed sleep and no causal evidence.

old_problem: The Procedure requests DMTF ResetType `PowerCycle`, while Criteria requires `ForceRestart`; the source supplies no approved precedence or exact-firmware equivalence mapping. A final `PowerState=On` cannot distinguish the two transitions. The supplied AI command also targets the wrong URI and weakens TLS/credential safety.
disposition_reason: Retain Pending and Source Conflict. DMTF defines `ForceRestart` as an immediate non-graceful restart and `PowerCycle` as power removal followed by restore; they are distinct reset semantics even though both can finish at PowerState On. ED-06/ED-18/ED-19 forbid conflating cycle classes or accepting final state alone. Only the platform owner can select the authoritative source term or provide version-bound firmware evidence that maps them equivalently. Static review can define discovery, one-shot safety, causal boot evidence and recovery, but cannot invent the required reset class.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1962, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, ED-01 through ED-30 and official DMTF reset semantics were read; the actual next queue row was directly opened as Functionality 1973 / Wistron-AMD SVM-00139-V004 / 3c7342bd75c3e7d8.
DMTF Redfish defines `ForceRestart` and `PowerCycle` as separate ResetType enum values with different transitions; a shared final On state does not prove equivalence.
The literal Procedure and Criteria are both coverage-bearing source fields, and no approved rule establishes that one silently overrides the other.
The action target and allowed ResetType must be discovered from the exact ComputerSystem action metadata; hardcoded `/Systems/system` cannot establish target identity or support.

A disruptive reset requires exact-SUT binding, workload drain, explicit just-in-time approval, one request, independent observation, changed boot identity and bounded recovery; timeout must never trigger an automatic retry.
No Redfish request, authentication, reset, power transition, host/BMC access, recovery, retry or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_command: BLOCKED — DO NOT EXECUTE until the owner selects the authoritative reset class. After unlock, discover the exact ComputerSystem and its Reset action target/AllowableValues over verified TLS; bind serial and baseline PowerState, reachability, boot ID and health. After unlock, the exact accepted one-shot action must produce the selected class's required causal transition, a changed boot identity, final approved PowerState and complete OS/platform recovery within the deadline, without unexpected health/log faults.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS is possible while `PowerCycle` versus `ForceRestart` remains unresolved. After unlock, PASS requires exact target/action/value support, one approved request, class-specific transition evidence, new boot ID, required final PowerState/OS readiness and clean health. FAIL on wrong/unsupported type, missing transition, unchanged boot identity, timeout, health regression or incomplete evidence. A 2xx response, final On state or fixed delay alone cannot PASS; end user owns verdict.

Observe independently; on timeout or anomaly preserve first evidence, do not retry or switch ResetType, and escalate through the approved recovery path.

Do not issue another reset or substitute a different ResetType. Use the approved independent console/BMC recovery and escalation path; quarantine the SUT until platform-owner review if state or boot identity is uncertain.
